dataset.title: Open Data Street Centerlines
dataset.description:
Line data of the approximate center-line for streets and roads in and surrounding the City of Greeley, CO is represented in this feature class. Exact spatial coverage of the data will vary as new developments are constructed. Data is actively reviewed quarterly as new roads are constructed/changed. Compiled by the City of Greeley. Used for Street Names, Street Classifications and road inventory.

Visit Greeley's accessibility site for assistance.

dataset.title: Open Data Mains and Culverts
dataset.description: This displays the locations and routes of stormwater mains and culverts within the City of Greeley. Storm mains are underground pipes that collect and transport stormwater runoff from streets and drainage basins to discharge points, helping to reduce flooding and erosion. Culverts are structures that allow stormwater to flow beneath roads or other barriers, maintaining natural drainage paths. The map includes details such as pipe size, material, flow direction, and condition. The spatial extent covers stormwater pipe features within Greeley city limits, and the data is used primarily by the Public Works, Stormwater Division. The dataset is maintained by the Stormwater Division.  For assistance with accessing the data please refer to City of Greeley's Accessibility Statement.

dataset.title: Public Parking
dataset.description:
This dataset consists of polygon features representing publicly accessible parking areas within the City of Greeley, Colorado. Each polygon delineates the approximate boundary of a parking facility such as a surface parking lot or designated public parking area. The dataset provides a spatial reference for identifying where public parking is available and for understanding how these facilities relate to nearby streets, buildings, parks, and other infrastructure.

The dataset is intended for use by municipal departments including public works, transportation planning, community development, parks, emergency management, and information technology. dataset.title: Downtown Development Authority DDA
dataset.description:

The dataset defines the geographic extent in which DDA programs, planning efforts, and development initiatives apply. dataset.title: Oil & Gas Wells
dataset.description:
This feature layer is a spatial dataset with a detailed view of oil and gas activity within Greeley’s Long-Range Expected Growth Area (LREGA) and includes various layers to support urban planning, emergency management, and regulatory oversight.

This dataset includes:

  • Oil & Gas Wells: Locations of active and historical oil and gas wells within the LREGA.

  • Use by Special Review (USR) Points & Areas: Identifies locations where special land-use permits have been granted for oil and gas development.

  • C.O.G.C.C. Fields & Wattenberg Field: Colorado Oil & Gas Conservation Commission (COGCC) designated oil and gas field boundaries, including the Wattenberg Field, a major oil and gas production area.

  • Fire Stations & Greeley Fire Response Areas: Provides fire station locations and service areas to assist with emergency response planning related to oil and gas activity.

  • Land and Legal Boundaries: Includes PLSS (Public Land Survey System) divisions, Quarter Sections, Sections, Township, and Range for reference.

  • LREGA Boundary: Defines the spatial extent of Greeley’s Long-Range Expected Growth Area to inform development and regulatory decisions.

  • 2.A. Parcels: Parcel data for land ownership and jurisdictional considerations.

This dataset is valuable for multiple departments, including Emergency Management, Fire Services, Community Development, Public Works, and Planning, as well as external agencies involved in environmental monitoring and regulatory compliance. It supports decision-making regarding oil and gas operations, emergency response planning, and future urban expansion. The dataset is updated regularly by Greeley IT to ensure accuracy and relevancy.

dataset.title: Voting Information
dataset.description: This dataset consists of two layers representing City of Greeley wards and Weld County precincts and supports the city clerks office. This dataset includes two geographic layers representing electoral boundaries within and around the City of Greeley. The Voting Precincts layer contains representations of voting precinct areas across Weld County, which are used to organize local elections, assign polling locations, and manage voter rolls. The Voting Wards layer delineates the official ward boundaries within the City of Greeley, which are used to elect City Council representatives and facilitate municipal governance. These layers provide spatial context for electoral processes and are important for community engagement, district-based services, and legal boundary verification. The dataset supports City departments for planning public notices, managing service areas, and understanding population distributions. The dataset is maintained and updated by Greeley IT GIS based on authoritative sources including the City Clerk’s office and Weld County election authorities. This dataset is valuable for departments such as City Clerks in communicating voting precinct and wards to the public. The data set is maintained by the Greeley IT GIS. For assistance with this product, please see Greeley's Accessibility Statement.

dataset.title: Greeley Fire Districts with Stations
dataset.description: The Greeley Fire Districts contains spatial data for fire service areas and stations within the City of Greeley, CO. Fire District Boundaries are the geographic polygons representing the areas served by various fire districts within the city and surrounding areas. Fire Stations Locations are points representing the physical locations of fire stations within the city. This data is crucial for planning the deployment of resources, assessing response times, and ensuring that emergency services are adequately distributed to meet the needs of the community.These boundaries are essential for emergency response planning and resource allocation, helping to define the service areas for firefighting and emergency medical services (EMS). This dataset is important for Emergency Management, Public Safety, and Fire Services departments in Greeley. It can assist in planning and coordinating response efforts, determining coverage areas, and improving the efficiency of fire and EMS operations. Additionally, the dataset supports planning efforts by Community Development, who may use the data for development approvals and infrastructure assessments near fire service zones. The data is updated regularly to reflect any changes in district boundaries. For assistance with this product, please see Greeley's Accessibility Statement.

dataset.title: Subdivisions
dataset.description:
This map image layer contains subdivision boundaries throughout Weld County and is sourced from Weld County’s GIS data hub. It is intended to support the City of Greeley Community Development Department with planning, permitting, zoning evaluation, and development review processes. Although the dataset is originally created and maintained by Weld County GIS, it is periodically updated and republished by Greeley IT GIS for local use. This version is used internally by departments that rely on current subdivision data for land use planning, infrastructure coordination, and development tracking within the Greeley municipal boundary and surrounding Weld County areas. Potential users include Community Development, Public Works, Stormwater, Parks, Forestry, Emergency Management (Police and Fire), and Finance, among others who require accurate subdivision boundaries for analysis or planning purposes. The dataset is reviewed for accuracy but may reflect the update cadence and data structure provided by Weld County. This dataset supports access to subdivision-related documents by linking PDF files to subdivision records for reference and review. It was created to provide centralized access to official subdivision documentation within GIS applications.

For assistance with accessing this product, please see https://greeleyco.gov/ada-policy-and-accessibility.

dataset.title: Tax Increment Financing (TIF) districts
dataset.description:
This feature layer represents the geographic boundaries of Tax Increment Financing (TIF) districts within the City of Greeley, CO. TIF districts are designated areas where tax revenue generated from increased property values is used to fund infrastructure improvements and economic development projects. The layer provides essential spatial information for financial analysts, community development planners, public works officials, and other stakeholders involved in urban planning and economic growth. Community Development can use this data to track redevelopment efforts, Public Works and Stormwater can assess infrastructure investments, and Finance can analyze tax revenue impacts. TIFs are updated as new TIF districts are established or modified. Users should verify boundaries with official city records for the most current information. 

For assistance with accessing this product, please see Greeley's https://greeleyco.gov/ada-policy-and-accessibility.
